title: Canonical Round Simulation
statement: Let $k,n$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c$ be a configuration with $k$ Boolean work tapes and $n+1$ possible states, and let $q$ be one of those states. Let $\mathrm{tr}$ be a transition rule assigning an action to each state, optional input bit, and tuple of optional work-tape bits; write $a$ for the action selected by $\mathrm{tr}$ from $q$ and the symbols scanned in $c$. For any output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, initialize the round machine with the encoded transition table, the output summary and unary encoding of $q$, both auxiliary heads at zero, and configuration data from $c$. There is a time $T$ with $0<T\le 50(L+1)$, where $L$ is the length of the encoded transition table, at which the round machine reaches the configuration built from applying $a$ to $c$, the new output summary and the unary encoding of the successor state (empty if it halts), with output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$ and auxiliary heads at zero. At every strictly intermediate positive time its state is neither the entry state nor the halt state, and at every time $u\le T$ its input head and each original work head lie at either their starting or finishing positions.
